summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The market steadied on the latest day after its sharp fall, but its mood stays stressed and its trend down. All five calls stay neutral with low conviction. Nothing here is expected to beat the index; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: After a big stumble, the whole field of runners caught its breath and walked a little. The brain does not guess who sprints next, because guessing did no better than luck before. It watches with pretend money, and the family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing to do today, and nothing to sell. The market steadied after its sharp fall, but its mood is still stressed. Monday's buy of the whole-market fund goes in as always; a weak patch means the same amount buys a bit more. Money we may need soon stays safe.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. The weekly bet game stood at two weeks won and one lost, and this week's bet looks set to lose, mostly because Monster fell hard on the latest day. Luck alone wins about half the weeks, so this means little.

Third, a lesson. A quiet day after a loud one feels like relief, but one calm day tells us no more than one bad day did. The plan does not change with the weather.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain

bets.why: This week's bet was already placed and is repeated unchanged: names above their trend passing every setup check, against names below their trend whose checklist leaned down. No rule like this has beaten luck, so it is a learning bet only.

pick.thesis: Alphabet edged up on the latest day but sits far below its high for the year and well below its fifty-day average, behind the benchmark on every window; the checklist reads mixed and calls it oversold. Its filing shows strong growth but thin free cash flow. The house rule says never to buy only because a stock fell a lot, and no tested rule shows that deep falls on this list bounce back. Berkshire's disclosed book holds it and is behind; that record is the firm's and too thin to count. Neutral and low, unchanged.
